edges.description: Loss of RB1-linked cell-cycle control contributes to bladder small cell oncogenesis, although the human evidence does not establish this as the sole or universal route to the tumor phenotype.
Smoking predisposes to the carcinoma, but the retained evidence does not establish a direct route from exposure to the recurrent TP53/RB1 lesions.

evidence.snippet: In the present study, we found that over 90% of bladder SmCC lacked RB1 expression on immunohistochemical analysis, suggesting that inactivation of the RB1 gene is a critical molecular alteration in development of SmCC.

nodes.description: Small cell bladder carcinomas frequently carry somatic alterations in TP53 and RB1. The downstream edge is limited to the established cell-cycle role of RB1 and does not imply that both alterations are universally required.
